catalog_quote: El acento léxico no tiene un carácter fonológico; de hecho, no se han encontrado pares mínimos acentuales. Existe evidencia tanto de acentuación oxítona (35) como de acentuación paroxítona (36) y proparoxítona (37). Leowen (1954) y Binder y Binder (1974) proponen una serie de reglas para lograr explicar la colocación del acento, las cuales se pueden reducir a dos principios: el primero, que la acentuación básica es paroxítona; el segundo (que explica la mayoría de las acentuaciones oxítonas), que el acento tiende a asignarse a la sílaba con más peso moraico, que para el caso del waunana son las sílabas cerradas (38), las sílabas con vocales largas (39) y, con un efecto variable, las sílabas con diptongos (40). ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation and the p. 25 cross-reference are verbatim in the extracted text we hold of Murillo & Marín 2022 at the stated section and pages (Acento, pp. 33-34, exx. 35-43; p. 25). (2) Deciding source: a 2022 open-access phonology article with its own recorded data (one speaker, acoustic analysis) that explicitly synthesises the two primary stress descriptions (Loewen 1954 thesis; Binder & Binder 1974, the only Glottolog phonology entry). No reference grammar or instrumental stress study of Wounaan exists in Glottolog's list or in Crossref; the classification (non-phonemic stress, default penult, CVC/CVV attract stress as a tendency, right edge, morphological attraction by suffixes) mirrors the source's hedged wording ('tiende a asignarse', 'efecto variable'). The held Arboleda 2008 phonology of the Colombian variety independently places stress in a final two-syllable window

sources.note: The listed open_url (sil.org/acpub/repository/, the volume's front matter) is 404 live and on the Internet Archive. The volume's only Waunana content is Binder's chapter, which SIL serves openly (archive 8809, file) and which was downloaded and scanned on 2026-09-16; The whole volume on archive.org (isbn_0883120623) is lending-only and its could not be reached by automated download. The chapter is a discourse study: 'prominence'/'prominent' occur only in the discourse-theme sense, and the scanned has no hit for stress/accent/tone.

sources.note: The primary Panamanian Waunana phonology whose stress rules our deciding source (Murillo & Marín 2022) compresses into 'default penult + heavy syllables attract stress'; reading the original rules would settle whether weight is stated categorically or as a tendency (our weight-hedged vs weight-sensitive choice) and what the diphthong 'variable effect' actually is.
